messages:
maria: heads up — ACME asked for a private-deploy upgrade path that preserves customer egress IPs and avoids a full cluster redeploy. they want a clear SLA and a minimal on-prem operator change. can we sketch options and launch gates?

aj: short answer: two viable paths. 1) operator-shim that swaps routing config at startup (no tenant data move). 2) rolling node replacement with a handoff step — heavier but simpler for netops.

luke: +1. operator-shim seems best for customers that cannot reassign public ips. risk: installers need ability to toggle eip-preserve mode and validate routing tables.

sasha: ACME will pay for a migration window but expects <1hr of traffic disruption. also they need audit logs showing egress-ip assignment history.

maria: proposed MVP scope: (a) installer flag `--preserve-egress-ip` that enables operator-shim mode, (b) preflight check that validates NAT/IGW mapping, (c) telemetry events for eip assignment. launch gate = preflight pass + 2 pilot customers.

aj: implementation note: operator-shim will patch the CNI config + add egress-preserve controller. rough config snippet for installer profile: ```yaml
installer:
  mode: onprem
  network:
    egress_preserve: true
    eip_claim_label: redwood.io/egress-claim
```

luke: need to confirm cloud-provider integrations: AWS (ENI + EIP), GCP (static IP on NAT), Azure (public ip assoc). i'll draft provider adapters.

devops-bot: deploy-checklist: created ticket INF-8213 "egress-preserve installer flag + operator-shim" — assign to @aj.

sasha: for contract language we should add an explicit rollback clause: if eip cannot be preserved, we revert to staged fallback (customer-consent required).

maria: good call. launch criteria checklist draft: 1) installer preflight OK on all three providers; 2) operator-shim automated tests + chaos run; 3) 2 pilot customers with SLA telemetry; 4) docs + runbook published. if any fail, gate stays closed.

aj: timeline estimate: 3 sprints for basic shim + tests; provider adapters another sprint. can we prioritize adapter for AWS first (most requests)?

luke: prioritize AWS, then GCP, then Azure. i'll pair with @aj on adapter API surface.

sasha: i'll schedule legal + support review for the rollback wording. also prepping customer comms template. :thumbsup:

maria: ok — next steps: aj to open PR with installer flag RFC, luke to prototype AWS adapter, sasha to draft contract addendum. weekly sync on Fri. thanks all.
